title: Nut-Free Brown Sugar Maple Cupcakes
shortDescription: Warm brown sugar maple cupcakes with a swirled cream frosting, ready in about 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a fall morning kitchen. Brown sugar and pure maple syrup team up for a warm, deep flavor that is not too sweet.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon in a medium bowl.
Beat butter and brown sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in maple syrup and vanilla.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with buttermilk. Start and end with flour. Mix just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Let cupcakes cool fully before frosting, about 45 minutes.
Beat butter for frosting on medium speed until smooth, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar in two batches.
Add heavy cream, maple syrup, and salt. Beat on high 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Load frosting into a piping bag fitted with a large star tip. Swirl frosting high onto each cooled cupcake.
tips: Use real maple syrup, not pancake syrup. It has a cleaner, deeper flavor.
Room temperature eggs and buttermilk mix into batter more smoothly, so pull them out early.
If your kitchen is warm, chill the frosting 10 minutes before piping so the swirl holds its shape.
Toast the cinnamon briefly in a dry pan before adding it, this wakes up the flavor.

faq.question: Can I use dark brown sugar instead of light brown sugar?
faq.answer: Yes. Dark brown sugar adds a stronger molasses note. The cupcakes will taste richer and slightly less sweet.

faq.question: Will this recipe work with maple extract instead of syrup?
faq.answer: Extract alone will not give the same moist texture. Use real syrup for the batter, and add a few drops of extract only if you want a stronger maple taste.

faq.question: How do I keep these cupcakes nut-free for a bake sale?
faq.answer: Check your buttermilk and vanilla labels for cross contamination warnings. Bake on a clean tray, away from any nut based treats.

faq.question: Can I make the frosting ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes. Store it covered in the fridge up to 3 days. Let it sit at room temperature and rebeat for 1 minute before piping.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring warm maple flavor to any table without any nut allergy worries. Bake a batch and see how fast they disappear.
